question_stem:
Fig. 8.1 shows a circuit that produces rectification of an alternating input voltage.
The input voltage V_{IN} is sinusoidal. The rectified output voltage V_{OUT} is applied across resistor R.
The variation of V_{IN} with time t has amplitude V_{0} and period T, as shown in Fig. 8.2.
The root-mean-square (r.m.s.) value of V_{IN} is 6.0 V.

The variation of $V_{\mathrm{IN}}$ with time t has amplitude $V_{0}$ and period T, as shown in Fig. 8.2.
The root-mean-square (r.m.s.) value of $V_{\mathrm{IN}}$ is 6.0 V.
